newsitem.title: LATVIA: TWO MEMBERS OF SECURITIES COMMISSION REJECTED.
newsitem.headline: TWO MEMBERS OF SECURITIES COMMISSION REJECTED.

text.p: Parliament's budget and finance committee on Tuesday backed three of the proposed candidates for the new securities commission and rejected two.
The committee's recommendations are not binding and are a recommendation only. Parliament has the final say and a vote is expected on May 8, politicians said.
The committee rejected economist and businessman Ojar Kehris and businessman Guntis Urlovksis.
They did not get backing as they were members of the commission which distributed credits from the G24, the granting of which is currently under investigation.

Finance Minister Robert Zile was negative on Kehris and Urlovskis. He said that personal interests of commission members should not conflict with their duties. He said that new candidates would only be considered after the parliament vote.
Kehris is chairman of the council of Ventspils Nafta and head of the Union of Economists 2000. Urlovskis is finance director of the Turiba consumer union.

The committee approved central bank vice-president Ilmar Rimshevics, privatisation agency legal director Viktor Shadinov and Latvian University international economic relations professor Andris Klaus.
